K10 Identity and versions (US-270-12a, US-270-13b). Automatos Cloud has no version flow for community items: submit_item writes version '1.0.0' every time (marketplace.py:833) and a resubmission is a NEW marketplace row (cloned_from_id = the submitter's workspace agent, :827); a Playbook resubmission with the same name is refused until the old row is removed (workflow_recipes.py:1395-1403) and is then a new row too (cloned_from_id :1432); no route edits a marketplace row (the agent and Playbook update routes take workspace rows only, workflow_recipes.py:561). So an item is keyed by its LINEAGE and versioned by its CONTENT. externalId = the first 32 hex of sha256('automatos-cloud:<type>:<lineage>') where lineage is 'from:<cloned_from_id>' when the row has one, else 'row:<natural key>' (an agent's public_id, core.py:287; a Playbook's template_id, :1374; a package's or plugin's slug): opaque, stable across resubmissions, never an id a route takes. version = the newest approved row's version; revision = the sha256 of the bundle's canonical bytes (K8). Locally ONE Cloud row per (type, externalId), updated in place when the revision moves (a row per version would list every version as its own card: list_items has no version grouping, marketplace.py:181-206), its version column set to local_version(version, revision). Every clone copies the version (cascade_installer.py:163; workflow_recipes.py:1543; package_installer._clone_recipe_to_workspace copies it reflectively, :281-289), so a workspace copy records what it was cloned from, and an update is a copy whose version differs from its Cloud row's (K17). A plugin is versioned by its own version (its files live under plugins/<slug>/<version>/, marketplace_s3.py:56-57): a changed revision with the same plugin version is refused ('a plugin changed without a new version'). An edge said in the docs: a submitter who deletes the workspace agent they submitted from (cloned_from_id ON DELETE SET NULL, core.py:310) starts a new lineage, so the next resubmission arrives as a new item.

userStories.title: An item written with a dependency that arrives in a later Sync is re-resolved, never frozen at its revision
userStories.description: As an operator, I want a Cloud agent whose plugin was still waiting, or a Cloud Playbook whose helper's bundle failed to fetch, to pick that dependency up on the next Sync, so that its install enables the plugin and finds its helper (PRD-270 §5.6, K13, K14, K15).
acceptanceCriteria: CAUSE: items_feed.changed_entries (orchestrator/services/marketplace_bundles/items_feed.py:182-193) treats an entry whose mapping is at the same revision as unchanged and never fetches it again, so an item written with an `unresolved` dependency stays unresolved until its OWN revision moves, even when the dependency arrives on the next Sync. (a) The item pass runs while plugins are 'waiting' (plugin_import.chosen_entries: AUTOMATOS_CLOUD_PLUGINS_PER_SYNC, default 5) or refused this Sync, so an agent naming such a plugin is written without its AgentAssignedPlugin rows and without that plugin's skills (import_agents.resolved_parts :187-205); on the next Sync the plugin is imported but the agent is unchanged, so cascade_agent_dependencies never enables the plugin for an install of it and its disclosure keeps saying the plugin is not on this install. sync_items.py's own docstring names the hazard ('an agent written without its plugins would keep them unresolved until its next revision') and guards only the plugin pass's FAILURE, not `waiting`. (b) A Playbook whose {item} agent's bundle fetch failed this Sync is written with needs_helper and agent_name 'a helper' (import_playbooks.helper_name :163-170: import_items.agent_names holds only this pass's fetched bundles) and an empty recommended_agents, so after the agent arrives on the next Sync the Playbook still installs with no helper for that step. → DONE — confirmed by reading the code: changed_entries skipped a same-revision mapping, upsert_agent/upsert_playbook returned UNCHANGED at once on a same revision, import_items.agent_names held only the pass's fetched bundles, and sync_items' docstring guarded only the plugin pass's failure. Fixed in commit 53465cd41 (see CHANGE).

CHANGE: an item whose mapping records a dependency a later Sync can bring (a plugin, a skill a plugin makes, a Playbook helper that is an {item} agent) is resolved again once it can be: either its bundle is fetched again at its revision and re-resolved in the item pass (counted unchanged unless its row changes), or an agent naming a plugin that is waiting or refused in this Sync is not written this Sync (counted, so it is new on the next one). Say which in the DONE mark. A row without a mapping and a workspace copy are still never read or written (K14); the one-transaction item pass and its advisory lock are unchanged; no new table, column or migration (K6). → DONE — chose the FIRST option: the bundle is fetched again at its revision and re-resolved in the item pass. (1) resolve.py records where a later Sync's dependency comes from on the mapping's unresolved entries (SOURCE_KEYS: a skill's plugin slug as 'package', a {item} helper's agent externalId as 'item'; disclosure.unresolved_of already strips both, so the web and Auto's card see {kind, name} as before); awaited() reads them back, held_now() finds what now resolves (approved active plugin, global active skill, mapped approved Cloud agent, or an agent bundle this Sync fetched), held_as_resolved()/at_revision() decide UNCHANGED. (2) items_feed.rechecked_entries names the entries held at their revision whose awaited dependency has arrived; nothing else is fetched again (a model or persona never triggers a refetch, and neither does a plugin still waiting). (3) sync_items.item_counts reads changed_entries, fetches those bundles, then reads rechecked_entries with the agent bundles just fetched as 'arriving' (so a helper whose bundle failed again doesn't trigger a refetch), fetches them through fetch_bundles (derived URL, sha256 = revision, strict validator); each mapping read ends in a rollback before any fetch (_mappings_read). (4) upsert_agent/upsert_playbook resolve first: UNCHANGED when the mapping is at the revision with the same unresolved; otherwise the existing update path (refusal checks, then links, row and mapping rewritten, version unchanged) counts UPDATED; a rewrite refused at the item's own revision, and a refetch that fails, leave it as it was and count unchanged. Rows without a mapping and workspace copies are still never read or written; import_items' one transaction, advisory lock and lock_timeout are unchanged; no table, column or migration. Judgement calls, from the code, security and database reviews: an item whose dependency arrived but whose rewrite stays refused (its name now held) is fetched again on each Sync and counted unchanged (one bundle GET each, bounded by the catalogue); a same-revision rewrite replaces the Cloud row's skills, apps and plugins as any update does (K14); mappings written before this commit carry no source keys, so only their plugins trigger a refetch (W2 is unreleased, so no data holds them). userStories.title: A plugin refused for a lasting reason never holds a Sync's plugin slots ahead of plugins that can import
userStories.description: As an operator, I want every plugin this install can import to arrive within a bounded number of Syncs, instead of waiting forever behind plugins it refuses every time (PRD-270 §5.6, K15).
acceptanceCriteria: CAUSE: plugin_import.chosen_entries (orchestrator/services/marketplace_bundles/plugin_import.py:200-205) takes the first AUTOMATOS_CLOUD_PLUGINS_PER_SYNC changed plugin entries by name, and changed_entries keeps every entry no mapping holds at its revision, including one refused last Sync for a reason that will not change: SLUG_HELD or NOT_ITS_SLUG (target_of :294-305), SAME_VERSION (its revision moved while its plugin version did not: the bundle carries the PluginCategory slug and icon and the scan's scannedAt, so POST /api/admin/plugins/backfill-categories or a category seed change on Automatos Cloud moves it), LINE_TOO_LONG (any text line over MAX_SCANNED_LINE 8192, e.g. a bundled or minified script), TOO_MANY_FINDINGS or CRITICAL_FINDING from this install's scan. Such a plugin is chosen again on every Sync, its bundle (and, for the scan refusals, its package up to PLUGIN_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB) downloaded again, and it holds a slot; with AUTOMATOS_CLOUD_PLUGINS_PER_SYNC of them sorting first by name, every plugin after them is counted 'waiting' on every Sync, for good, and so (P270W2-RVW-1) are the agents that need them. → DONE — confirmed by reading plugin_import.py at dc2233c53: chosen_entries took the first AUTOMATOS_CLOUD_PLUGINS_PER_SYNC changed plugin entries by name before any check, and held_target/target_of ran inside checked_plugin only for those, so a SLUG_HELD, NOT_ITS_SLUG or SAME_VERSION plugin (kept by changed_entries, since no mapping holds it at its revision) took a place on every Sync, and a package the scan refused was downloaded again on every Sync ahead of plugins not yet tried. Fixed in commit 1e9f63f23 (see CHANGE).

CHANGE: a refusal decidable from the bundle and this install's rows (held_target/target_of: SLUG_HELD, NOT_ITS_SLUG, SAME_VERSION) never takes one of the per-Sync slots: the target is decided before the cap, which bounds package downloads only; and a plugin whose package was refused at a revision is not downloaded again at that revision ahead of a plugin not yet tried (for example, the process remembers each refused (externalId, revision) and orders those after the rest). Every importable plugin is then imported within ceil(importable / AUTOMATOS_CLOUD_PLUGINS_PER_SYNC) Syncs. K15's checks, their order before any byte is stored, and K10's SAME_VERSION refusal itself are unchanged; no new table, column or migration (K6); `plugins.waiting` counts only plugins that could import. → DONE — import_plugins now fetches every new or changed plugin's bundle (fetch_bundles: the derived URL, sha256 = revision, the strict validator) and runs K15's slug check (held_target/target_of) on each in targeted_plugins BEFORE the cap; a plugin it refuses (SLUG_HELD, NOT_ITS_SLUG, SAME_VERSION, NOT_READ, or anything unforeseen: logged, its read rolled back) is counted refused and takes no place. chosen_plugins orders the rest by place_order (name, then externalId; a plugin this process refused once it held a place, at that revision, after every other) and the first AUTOMATOS_CLOUD_PLUGINS_PER_SYNC download their packages; the rest wait, so plugins.waiting counts only plugins whose slug check passed. The process remembers each refused (externalId, revision) in remember_refused/refused_before (a BoundedCache(1) holding a frozenset, the services/themes/bounded_cache.py idiom W1's catalogue snapshot uses; W1's one-Sync lock serialises it; pruned each pass to the entries still new or changed, so bounded by the catalogue; a restart forgets). checked_plugin takes the Targeted (the bundle and the target decided before the cap) and keeps K15's order: the package from the derived URL, the zip rules, manifest.json, the static scan, then the rows read again (CHANGED_HERE, or target_of's own refusal) before any byte is stored. K10's SAME_VERSION refusal is unchanged; no table, column or migration. Judgement calls, from the code, security and database reviews: (1) the cap bounds package downloads only, as the AC says, so every new or changed plugin's bundle is read on each Sync: a lasting slug refusal costs one bundle GET (at most AUTOMATOS_CLOUD_BUNDLE_MAX_KB) per Sync, bounded by W1's 1000-item catalogue, the item pass's accepted cost (RVW-1); said in the module docstring and the docs; (2) a cap of 0 still requests nothing and counts every new or changed plugin waiting (config.py: 0 downloads none; test_prd270w2_re_resolve and test_prd270w2_sync_routes pin it), so at 0 waiting is not limited to plugins that could import; (3) every refusal after a plugin took a place is remembered, a transient one included (PACKAGE_NOT_FETCHED on a network failure, NOT_STORED, NOT_SAVED, CHANGED_HERE): it comes last but is still tried whenever a place is free, a delay and never a block; (4) ceil(importable / cap) holds for slug refusals, while a package refused for the first time at a revision takes a place once (it must be downloaded to be refused); the memory is per backend process (the local compose runs one worker, as W1's in-process Sync lock assumes), and a hostile catalogue that rotates revisions can still make its plugins look untried; (5) an AUTOMATOS_CLOUD_URL that isn't an origin now counts every new or changed plugin refused (none can be fetched) and none waiting; (6) two entries naming one slug both pass the early check: the second downloads its package and the rows read again refuse it before any byte is stored.
